  - helpful 132/139 (core 83/83);

  cost for the fresh set plus dev ×3: $4.20 at published rates.

  They are not integrated with production storage. **Step 4 (judging) is not built** on the clean path, so nothing yet shows the clean

     a likely cause, with no fix proven. Alex approved designing a protected link check through the council; a first draft was stopped
     because it would drop founding premises and contrary facts.

Jev's comparison input still carries the model's text without the mark; changing it changes measured Step 2 behaviour and needs its own measurement.
  5. **The lidar policy thesis** recurs at the boundary (one dev draw in three).

**Clean Step 1 source investigation (2026-11-07):** A [source-loss census](../clean-arch/STEP1-SOURCE-LOSS-CENSUS.md) traces two separate losses in the historical cleaner and records reproducible corpus observations. Offline candidate comparisons expose both recovered content and source-identity or contamination risks. A subsequent [full-page diagnostic](../clean-arch/STEP1-FULL-PAGE-RESULTS.md) completed 102 calls on 17 selected articles and independent source-backed review. The [council regroup](../clean-arch/STEP1-SOURCE-REGROUP-COUNCIL.md) and [source-preservation design](../clean-arch/STEP1-SOURCE-PRESERVATION-DESIGN.md) describe an isolated candidate checked against all 34,084 records, with a fake-answer actual-runner handoff and provenance display in the replay renderer. ## 5. Step 2: find and compare related evidence

### Why this is separate

An open thesis may accumulate many evidence records. Step 1 needs to understand the article and the open research; it does not need to read every prior statement to do that. Step 2 uses each proposed `{thesis, evidence}` association to find the history worth comparing.

### Find candidate evidence

The proposed design places semantic search over the evidence library. It uses the thesis and incoming evidence to find top-N related evidence across the current entity, including evidence linked to other theses. The thesis is search context, not a restriction to evidence already linked to that thesis. This also applies when the proposed thesis is new. For example, “raised its revenue outlook” and “expects higher sales” can be related despite different wording. Alex chose this entity-wide scope on 2026-11-06.

Search returns **candidates**, not a final decision. Alex discussed a starting point of top 10; the implementation and quality requirements need to be measured.

A match outside the returned set will not be considered by the comparison. Search quality therefore matters independently from the model's ability to compare the records it receives.

### Compare with Jev

**2026-11-08 (candidate, [round log](step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/LOG.md) §§24, 31–35):**
- Comparison reads the full passages; the 600-character cut is removed.
- An unlinked record also searches by its own text.
- `figures` never enter a search or comparison text.
- Jev is asked the clean path's own piece question, aligned with line 2's test: a repeat reports the stored piece's main statement, and
  an official's denial of a report is a revision.
- When a thesis opens, every stored unlinked group from earlier articles is judged against it in batches of ten (a yes/no question; the
  company's overall results inform only a revenue or earnings thesis). Each judged pair is recorded once.
- On c6's records: search 97.9%, wrong merges 1.9% (2 of 104), both lines met; line 3 not re-measured.

Jev compares the new evidence with the returned evidence. The intended outcomes are:

| Outcome | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Repeat | The new material presents the same statement again. | Another article reports the same company forecast. |
| Revision | A later account changes the same statement. | The company revises its forecast from 12% to 25%. |
| New evidence | It is not identified as a repeat or revision of the evidence compared. | A different analyst offers a separate forecast. |

The words, amount, speaker, source and time can matter to the comparison. A later statement about the same subject is not necessarily a revision. A matching amount alone does not prove that two statements are the same.

The result “new evidence” is the outcome of the comparison performed; it is not proof that no matching evidence exists elsewhere in the library. When the incoming evidence is judged a repeat of several candidates, it joins only the group Jev judges it most like: the highest same-statement probability, with ties going to the earliest group (Alex, 2026-11-08). A comparison that fails is not saved and is reported.

**Repeat handoff:** when Jev identifies a repeat, the comparison must retain the identity of the existing evidence record it was compared against. Step 3 uses that identity to place the incoming record in the existing record's group, adding its source and any missing thesis link. The typed Jev response need not generate the record ID: the caller can associate the choice with the candidate it supplied. The rule for several matching candidates is stated above.

**Step 2 acceptance (Alex, 2026-11-08).** Three lines apply:
1. For incoming evidence whose earlier version is in the library, search returns it at least 90% of the time.
2. At most 2% of merges are clearly wrong.
3. Grouped dossiers keep no fewer details added by later reports than no merging does.

The first measurement against these lines is in the [Step 2 log](step2-validation-2026-11-07/LOG.md) §12; the isolated modules are `step2/compare.py` and `step3/library.py`.

The diagram's intended sequence is: use `{thesis, incoming evidence}` to search the evidence library; pass the returned candidates and incoming evidence to Jev; pass the comparison result and the proposed association to Step 3. For a new thesis, search the same entity-wide evidence library. A concrete working draft of the Jev comparison request appears in [section 13](#13-step-2-prompt-jev-working-draft).

## 6. Step 3: save evidence and links

Step 3 takes the proposals from Step 1 and the comparison outcomes from Step 2 and writes the resulting research information.

| Result | What is saved |
|---|---|
| New thesis with supporting evidence | The new thesis and its evidence link; save new evidence or reuse a matching record according to Step 2. |
| New evidence for an existing thesis | The evidence and its link to the thesis. |
| Repeat | Place the incoming record in the existing evidence record's group: add its source and any missing link to the relevant thesis, and keep the incoming record's own text and fields inside the group. Do not rewrite the existing record, and do not create a separate evidence record for the same statement. |
| Revision | The new evidence and its source, linked to the earlier statement as a revision. |

A revision does not erase the earlier statement. On 2026-11-06, Alex chose to keep one evidence record for a repeat and add the new source and any missing thesis link. On 2026-11-08 the Step 2 validation showed that keeping only the earlier text discards details a later report adds, such as a guidance condition; Alex then chose to keep each repeat's own text and source inside the stored record's group, without rewriting the original ("A 继续；跑council loop 开始做"; [Step 2 log](step2-validation-2026-11-07/LOG.md) §7). How a judgement reads a group is being tested. Multiple articles reporting the same statement do not automatically establish independent original sources. The current production writer stores separate repeat records, so this is a change for the clean path and needs implementation and verification; the existing historical records remain available. Step 3 ends when the chosen thesis, evidence and relationships are saved. How they are physically stored and written is a separate implementation decision.

(summary, passages, party, statement date, period), cosine similarity of embeddings, top 10; a record with no association, or one that

TOP = 10


def stated(record):
    return record['statement_date'] or record.get('statement_date_text') or 'unknown'


def doc_text(record):
    return '\n'.join([record['summary'], ' '.join(record['passages']), f"party: {record['original_party'] or 'unknown'}",
                      f"stated: {stated(record)}", f"period: {record['evidence_period'] or 'unknown'}"])


def query_text(record, thesis_question):
    return f"thesis: {thesis_question}\n{record['summary']}\n{' '.join(record['passages'])}"


def piece_text(record, label):
    return (f"{label} [{record['tier']}; {record['reporting_speaker']}; original source {record['original_party']}, stated "
            f"{stated(record)}] {record['summary']} | quote: {' '.join(record['passages'])}")


def query_vectors(vectors, record, thesis_questions):
    """The search queries of one record, in order: one per thesis association, then its own text when it has no association or lists
    the company's figures."""
    queries = [vectors[query_text(record, thesis_questions[t])] for t in record['thesis_ids']]
    if not record['thesis_ids'] or record.get('figures'):
        queries.append(vectors[doc_text(record)])
    return queries


# Jev's piece criteria aligned with the Step 2 merge line's own test (PRD §5 line 2; AGENTS §7.1, one ruler): a repeat is a later report
# of the stored piece's main statement. Production's wording (views/jev_matching.PIECES) judged "the same evidence", so a later report of
# only a secondary statement inside a stored record (an official's denial carried in the report it denies) was merged as a repeat.
PIECES = {'same_statement': "the INCOMING PIECE reports the STORED PIECE's main statement: a retelling, another outlet carrying it, the "
                            "same number in text or a table, or the same speaker repeating it; wording, precision and extra detail may "
                            "differ. If the stored piece carries several statements and the incoming piece reports only a secondary one, "
                            "this is not it",
          'supersedes': "a later version of the stored piece's main statement, changed: the same speaker revises that guidance, "
                        "forecast or event-progress statement, an official confirms or denies that reported claim, or the original "
                        "source revises it; another statement on the same topic is not this",
          'different': "a different fact, figure or matter, a figure for another period or quantity, or only a secondary statement of "
                       "the stored piece, even if on the same topic"}


def piece_question(text):
    return {'type': 'choice', 'criteria': PIECES,
            'instructions': 'How does the INCOMING PIECE relate to the STORED PIECE below? Use only the supplied text. STORED PIECE:\n' + text}


INFORMS = {'true': "the STORED PIECE bears on the THESIS's own matter (the parties, products, policy or quantity the THESIS names) and "
                   "makes its answer more or less likely, as evidence filed under it would",
           'false': "the STORED PIECE concerns another matter, or is a company-wide result or event that does not speak to the THESIS's "
                    "own matter, or would not change its answer"}


def informs_question(text):
    return {'type': 'noul', 'criteria': INFORMS,
            'instructions': 'Does the STORED PIECE below inform the THESIS stated above? Use only the supplied text; a shared company, '
                            'product family or word is not enough, and the company\'s overall results, guidance and estimates inform a '
                            'thesis about its revenue or earnings path, not one about a competitor, a supplier or a policy unless they '
                            'speak to it. STORED PIECE:\n' + text}


def later_link_judge(library, thesis_question, ask):
    """The judge `Library.link_later` calls: one Jev request per batch, the thesis as state, one yes/no question per stored group."""
    def judge(group_ids):
        questions = {f'q{i}': informs_question(piece_text(library.groups[g]['original'], 'STORED PIECE')) for i, g in enumerate(group_ids)}
        raw = ask(f'THESIS: {thesis_question}', questions)
        return {g: raw[f'q{i}']['noul'] >= jev_matching.THRESHOLD for i, g in enumerate(group_ids)}
    return judge


def cosine(a, b):
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b)) / (math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a)) * math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b)) or 1)


def search(library, vectors, record, thesis_questions):
    """Candidate group ids: each query's top 10 by cosine against the groups' original records, merged in rank order."""
    candidates = []
    for query in query_vectors(vectors, record, thesis_questions):
        ranked = sorted(library.order, key=lambda g: -cosine(query, vectors[doc_text(library.groups[g]['original'])]))[:TOP]
        candidates += [g for g in ranked if g not in candidates]
    return candidates


def outcome(answers, order):
    """answers: {group id: {'choice', 'probabilities'}}; order: group ids in creation order."""
    same = [g for g, a in answers.items() if a['choice'] == 'same_statement']
    later = [g for g, a in answers.items() if a['choice'] == 'supersedes']
    if same:
        best = max(same, key=lambda g: (answers[g]['probabilities']['same_statement'], -order.index(g)))
        return {'kind': 'repeat', 'repeat_of': [best], 'revises': later}
    if later:
        return {'kind': 'revision', 'revises': later}
    return {'kind': 'new'}


def forward(articles, library, vectors, thesis_questions, ask, workers=8, opened=None):
    """articles: lists of Step 3 records in article order. ask(state, questions) returns Jev's answers by question id, or raises.
    opened: per article, the thesis ids it opened; after the article's records are written, each is linked later to the stored groups
    that arrived unlinked from earlier articles (`Library.link_later`). A thesis written to with pairs still pending is judged again,
    against its opening boundary. Returns one decision per record."""
    decisions = []
    for index, records in enumerate(articles):
        def decide(record):
            candidates = search(library, vectors, record, thesis_questions)
            if not candidates:
                return record, candidates, {}, {'kind': 'new'}
            questions = {f'q{i}': piece_question(piece_text(library.groups[g]['original'], 'STORED PIECE'))
                         for i, g in enumerate(candidates)}
            incoming = piece_text(record, 'INCOMING PIECE')
            try:
                raw = ask(incoming, questions)
            except Exception as first:   # retried once; a second failure is reported, never silently saved as new
                try:
                    raw = ask(incoming, questions)
                except Exception as error:
                    return record, candidates, {}, {'kind': 'failed', 'reason': f'{type(first).__name__}: {first}; retry: {type(error).__name__}: {error}'}
            answers = {g: {'choice': raw[f'q{i}']['choice'], 'probabilities': raw[f'q{i}']['probabilities']} for i, g in enumerate(candidates)}
            return record, candidates, answers, outcome(answers, library.order)
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(decide, records))
        for record, candidates, answers, result in results:
            entry = {'id': record['id'], 'candidates': candidates, 'answers': answers, 'outcome': result}
            try:
                entry['group'] = library.apply(record, result)
            except Exception as error:
                entry['refused'] = f'{type(error).__name__}: {error}'
            decisions.append(entry)
        article = records[0]['article'] if records else None
        if article is None:
            continue
        written = {t for r in records for t in r['thesis_ids']}
        retry = [t for t in written if t in library.pending and t not in (opened[index] if opened else [])]
        for thesis_id in list(opened[index] if opened else []) + retry:   # opened here, or written to with pairs still pending
            result = library.link_later(thesis_id, later_link_judge(library, thesis_questions[thesis_id], ask), article)
            library.later_log.append({'thesis': thesis_id, 'article': article, **result})
    return decisions
"""Isolated Step 3 evidence library for the clean path (PRD §6): an in-memory logical store and its dossier text, not the live writer.

A group is one stored statement. Its original record keeps its id and fields unchanged and gives the group its id. A later record that
Step 2 judged a repeat joins the group as a member and keeps its own id, text, fields and source article. Thesis links belong to the
group and remember the record that brought each one. A revision is its own group, linked to every group it revises; a repeat that also
revises another group adds that link to its own group, naming the member that established it.

The writer refuses rather than guesses: a failed comparison, several repeat targets, an unknown group, or a replayed record whose
placement differs from the first time raise `Refused` and write nothing. Physical storage and crash recovery are not provided here.

Later linking (Alex, 2026-11-08: a material statement no thesis takes is kept and linked when a related thesis opens; design
STEP1-CONDITIONS-DESIGN.md §§11.1, 17): when a thesis opens, every group whose original arrived with no link, from an earlier article,
is judged against it in batches. Each judged (thesis, group) pair is recorded once in `judged`; a batch that fails twice stays pending,
is reported, and is judged again on the next write to that thesis, against the same opening boundary (`opened_at`)."""
import copy

RECORD_FIELDS = ('id', 'article', 'publisher', 'publication_date', 'summary', 'passages', 'original_party', 'reporting_speaker', 'tier',
                 'statement_date', 'evidence_period', 'thesis_ids')


class Refused(Exception):
    """A Step 2 outcome the library will not write; nothing was changed."""


class Library:
    def __init__(self):
        self.groups = {}       # group id → {'original': record, 'members': [record], 'links': {thesis id: record id}, 'revises': [{'group', 'by'}]}
        self.placement = {}    # record id → group id
        self.order = []        # group ids in the order they were created
        self.judged = {}       # (thesis id, group id) → True | False, the later-linking ledger
        self.later_log = []    # one entry per later-linking call: thesis, article, linked, pending, judged
        self.opened_at = {}    # thesis id → the article that opened it: the boundary of its later linking
        self.pending = {}      # thesis id → group ids whose judgement failed twice and waits for the next write to the thesis

    def apply(self, record, outcome):
        """Write one record with its Step 2 outcome: {'kind': 'new' | 'repeat' | 'revision' | 'failed', 'repeat_of': [group ids],
        'revises': [group ids], 'reason': text}. Returns the id of the group that holds the record."""
        missing = [f for f in RECORD_FIELDS if f not in record]
        if missing:
            raise Refused(f'record lacks {missing}')
        kind, repeat_of, revises = outcome['kind'], list(outcome.get('repeat_of') or []), list(outcome.get('revises') or [])
        if kind == 'failed':
            raise Refused(f"comparison failed for {record['id']}: {outcome.get('reason', 'no reason given')}")
        if kind not in ('new', 'repeat', 'revision'):
            raise Refused(f'unknown outcome {kind!r}')
        if (kind == 'repeat') != bool(repeat_of) or len(repeat_of) > 1:
            raise Refused(f"a repeat names exactly one group; got {repeat_of} for outcome {kind}")
        if kind == 'revision' and not revises:
            raise Refused('a revision names the group it revises')
        for group_id in repeat_of + revises:
            if group_id not in self.groups:
                raise Refused(f'unknown group {group_id}')
        target = repeat_of[0] if repeat_of else record['id']
        if record['id'] in self.placement:
            if self.placement[record['id']] != target:
                raise Refused(f"{record['id']} was placed in {self.placement[record['id']]}, not {target}")
            group = self.groups[target]
            stored = next(r for r in [group['original']] + group['members'] if r['id'] == record['id'])
            if {k: v for k, v in stored.items() if k != 'thesis_ids'} != {k: v for k, v in record.items() if k != 'thesis_ids'}:
                raise Refused(f"{record['id']} names a stored record with different content; a changed record needs a new id")
            self._link(group, record)
            return target
        if kind == 'repeat':
            group = self.groups[target]
            group['members'].append(copy.deepcopy(record))
        else:
            group = {'original': copy.deepcopy(record), 'members': [], 'links': {}, 'revises': []}
            self.groups[target] = group
            self.order.append(target)
        self.placement[record['id']] = target
        self._link(group, record)
        for revised in revises:
            if revised != target and not any(r['group'] == revised for r in group['revises']):
                group['revises'].append({'group': revised, 'by': record['id']})
        return target

    def link_later(self, thesis_id, judge, before_article, batch=10):
        """Judge every group whose original arrived unlinked from an article before `before_article` against a newly opened thesis.
        judge(group ids) returns {group id: True | False} or raises. Returns {'linked': [...], 'pending': [...], 'judged': n}."""
        self.opened_at.setdefault(thesis_id, before_article)
        before_article = self.opened_at[thesis_id]
        todo = [g for g in self.order if not self.groups[g]['original']['thesis_ids']
                and self.groups[g]['original']['article'] < before_article and (thesis_id, g) not in self.judged]
        linked, pending = [], []
        for start in range(0, len(todo), batch):
            ids = todo[start:start + batch]
            answers = None
            for _attempt in range(2):
                try:
                    answers = judge(ids)
                    break
                except Exception:   # tried twice, then reported as pending, never saved as a judgement
                    answers = None
            if answers is None:
                pending += ids
                continue
            for group_id in ids:
                self.judged[(thesis_id, group_id)] = bool(answers[group_id])
                if answers[group_id]:
                    self.groups[group_id]['links'].setdefault(thesis_id, self.groups[group_id]['original']['id'])
                    linked.append(group_id)
        if pending:
            self.pending[thesis_id] = pending
        else:
            self.pending.pop(thesis_id, None)
        return {'linked': linked, 'pending': pending, 'judged': len(todo) - len(pending)}

    @staticmethod
    def _link(group, record):
        for thesis_id in record['thesis_ids']:
            group['links'].setdefault(thesis_id, record['id'])

    @staticmethod
    def articles(group):
        """Distinct source articles of a group, oldest first; two records from one article count once."""
        seen = []
        for record in [group['original']] + group['members']:
            if record['article'] not in seen:
                seen.append(record['article'])
        return seen

    def dossier(self, thesis_id):
        """Group ids linked to a thesis, in creation order."""
        return [g for g in self.order if thesis_id in self.groups[g]['links']]


def labelled_passages(record):
    """Each passage as a reader sees it: the source text Step 1 found, labelled 'Quote', or, when Step 1 did not find it (verified
    value None), the model's text labelled 'Unverified quote'. The model's own text stays in the record's `passages`. A record stored
    before verification was carried shows its passages as 'Quote'."""
    verified = record.get('verified_passages') or record['passages']
    return [('Quote', found) if found is not None else ('Unverified quote', passage) for passage, found in zip(record['passages'], verified)]


def record_text(record, label):
    attribution = record['original_party'] or 'unknown party'
    if record['reporting_speaker'] and record['reporting_speaker'] != record['original_party']:
        attribution += f", reported by {record['reporting_speaker']}"
    head = (f"[{label}] {record['publication_date']} · {record['publisher'] or 'unknown publisher'} · {attribution} · tier {record['tier']}"
            f" · stated {record['statement_date'] or 'unknown'} · period {record['evidence_period'] or 'unknown'}")
    quotes = '\n'.join(f'  {label_of}: "{p}"' for label_of, p in labelled_passages(record))
    return f"{head}\n  {record['summary']}\n{quotes}"


def group_text(library, group_id, label, labels, member_text=True, notes=()):
    """A group as a reader sees it: the original record, then each later report of the same statement in arrival order, with its own
    text when `member_text` is set and as a source line otherwise. Distinct articles are counted; repeats are not called confirmation."""
    group = library.groups[group_id]
    lines = [record_text(group['original'], label)]
    if group['members']:
        articles = library.articles(group)
        publishers = {r['publisher'] for r in [group['original']] + group['members']}
        lines.append(f'  Later reports of the same statement: {len(group["members"])} records from {len(articles) - 1} further articles '
                     f'({len(publishers)} publishers in all). Articles repeating a statement do not by themselves confirm it independently.')
        for member in group['members']:
            if member_text:
                party = '' if member['original_party'] == group['original']['original_party'] else f" · {member['original_party']}"
                quotes = ' '.join(f'"{p}"' if kind == 'Quote' else f'"{p}" (unverified)' for kind, p in labelled_passages(member))
                lines.append(f"    - {member['publication_date']} · {member['publisher']}{party}: {member['summary']}\n      Quote: {quotes}")
            else:
                lines.append(f"    - {member['publication_date']} · {member['publisher']}")
    for revised in group['revises']:
        lines.append(f"  Revises [{labels[revised['group']]}]." if revised['group'] in labels else '  Revises an entry outside this dossier.')
    lines += [f'  {note}' for note in notes]
    return '\n'.join(lines)

# Step 2: should Jev see retrieval scores?

Research council, 2026-11-08. Scope: the isolated clean Step 2 evidence-comparison path. No production change, model test, or change to the concurrent Step 1 experiment.

## Conclusion

Neither a benefit nor harm has been established. Keep the present request until a controlled comparison shows an advantage. Similarity is calculated between a search query and a stored group's original text; it is not a probability of same statement. The query may contain a thesis and a candidate may have several scores from different queries. Jev does not receive these scores; it receives the incoming piece as state and one candidate per typed question. It returns a choice and probabilities. Jev's choice probability, not cosine, selects among multiple same-statement results.

## Concrete observation

In saved c6 X4, incoming 12:e1 was grouped into 1:E1 although the two revenue-sharing arrangements were judged different. Recomputed from the cached exact-text vectors, cosine of the one thesis query against 1:E1's document is 0.8574. Its own document-vector cosine is 0.8654, but the record had one thesis query and that value was not its retrieval query. The saved Jev answer called same_statement at 0.89. This is one error; it neither establishes that score information will harm Jev nor measures a score distribution. Source: `poc/data/clean-step2-forward-c6-2026-11-08/{decisions.json,library.json,embeddings.json,merge-key.json,merge-third-answer.json}`. Query/doc text and cosine are reconstructed as `clean-arch/step2/compare.py` defines them.

## Council

Claude Code session 4c06c24f-8f77-4add-9443-7081a27b7903; original handoff, streams, stderr and challenge are saved alongside this record. Claude initially recommended an offline score-separation gate. Codex challenged it: overlapping marginal scores cannot rule out conditional help, and separation cannot establish Jev uses them. Claude agreed and withdrew that gate, its extrapolation of score ranges from another task, and claims about Jev's internal reasoning. Offline profiling can inform a test but cannot establish efficacy. Vendor describes Jev as a typed, non-text-generating decision model with independently evaluated questions (https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction); evidence on LLM anchoring is only a hypothesis for Jev, not a finding (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.01724).

## Proposed discriminating test, not yet registered or run

Reconstruct identical saved candidate requests; interleave fresh no-score controls with true-score requests and a score-shuffled control, with fixed score representation and randomization, repeated draws, cache misses, and identical model, candidates and question content except score lines. Make each score's query origin explicit: multiple search queries may yield different scores. A shuffled control tests sensitivity to a number but needs care with singleton/equal-score cases and preserving query origin. A source-blind independent reader judges differing pairs and controls without seeing arm, score, or prior decision. Report wrong merges, missed repeats, incorrect revision classifications and group choices separately, all cases, with same-arm variability, cost and limitations; fixed-candidate comparisons do not prove forward-run performance. The fresh set has few or no revisions; use separately identified stored revision cases without presenting isolated pair results as product-path evidence. Freeze design, audit and preflight under repository rules before any paid send. A score can also encode context Jev did not directly receive (e.g. thesis wording or period), so improvement would not itself establish the mechanism.

No evidence supports a universal score threshold. This proposal does not alter the accepted configuration or authorize deployment.
# Council: the fresh Step 2 wrong merge (X22)

Read-only council, 2026-11-09. Codex and Claude Code independently traced the sources, the stored Jev request and answer, the Step 3 group and the reader's text; challenge round in `round2.jsonl`. Original user-requested scope: this one error, no product or ruler edits, no paid model calls.

## What happened

The earlier 2026-09-05 Motley Fool source reported that Vera Rubin was in production and that management expected it to represent about 20% of Q3 data-centre revenue. The later 2026-09-06 Calcalist source reported that Nvidia said Vera Rubin systems were commercially delivered in August. The two source articles are preserved in `reports/step2-score-council-2026-11-08/blind-packets.json`, case 9 candidate C7 (key in blind-key.json); these are media reports, not the primary earnings-call transcript.

Archived request for incoming 22:ev-11 against 13:e4 asked Jev to compare their source-backed text. It chose same_statement at 0.49, different 0.36, supersedes 0.15. `clean-arch/step2/compare.py:109` acts on the chosen label without a 0.5 floor, so the incoming record joined 13:e4. Retrieval found this candidate. The model provides no textual explanation; the reason for the choice is unproven.

The fresh merge review classified the two as different, and a third classified the merge wrong. Independent Codex review agrees; earlier Claude blind review called it overlap, and a separate Claude adjudicator called it different. Thus whether it is a clearly wrong merge rather than an overlap depends on reader judgment. We agree the delivery is not a straightforward repeat of the production statement and revenue forecast. The prior acceptance reference grouped underlying article matters as a later step and marked the delivery revision; that reference uses a broader revision concept than Step 2's comparison, and its unit is the article matter, not necessarily the system record. The most natural reading under the current comparison contract is a separate new statement; revision is a plausible interpretation of the milestone depending on the meaning of 'changed event-progress statement'. The primary statement of the original bundled production-and-forecast record is not formally identified. No change to the reference or contract is proposed.

## Actual and potential impact

The clean prototype group retains the delivery record's own summary, quote and source as a member. Offline calling `group_text` on the saved group produces the label 'Later reports of the same statement' above that member: misleading grouping and label, not observed text deletion. The acceptance did not test whether this group changed a reader's investment judgment; Step 4 of this clean path was not built for this run. The production writer and live application were not changed. If a future reader treats group members as restatements, it could underweight a new milestone; that downstream consequence is a risk, not an observed result. The first article attributes the 20% forecast to management but does not explicitly attribute production status to Nvidia; its stored summary does, an attribution difference in this case without an established census.

## A tempting threshold

An offline read of the 57 saved merges showed 2 selected repeats below 0.5: X22 at 0.49 (judged wrong by the original merge readers) and X47 at 0.47 (accepted by both original readers; Broadcom revenue forecasts). A 0.5 floor on this fixed draw would remove one wrong merge and one accepted merge. This is not a root cause proof or general performance measurement. No threshold change is recommended from this single comparison; old production code uses such a floor, while the clean prototype does not, and no decision about adding it to the clean path was established here.

Relevant records: `poc/data/clean-acceptance-2026-11-09/step2/decisions.json`, `library.json`, `jev.sqlite`, `merge-third-answer.json`; `poc/data/clean-acceptance-2026-11-09/settled.json` and `prerun-prompt.md`; `clean-arch/step3/library.py`; `clean-arch/step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/LOG.md` §§43–44. The independent Codex review is `codex-review.md`. One full fresh test produced 1 clear wrong merge of 57 by its readers; this council did not reclassify its immutable result.
# Step 2 wrong-merge council: candidate direction, not a proven fix

2026-11-09. Alex requested a council to think through a general fix. Codex and Claude independently read the saved requests, source-backed records, decisions, current contracts and prior trials, challenged each other's proposals, and converged after further challenges. This is a read-only investigation; no model experiment, production/configuration change, new ruler, or change to the concurrent end-to-end run was made. Streams and handoffs are preserved in this directory.

## What was found

In one fresh draw and three dev draws, 363 accepted-as-repeat outcomes received recorded reviews: 316 accepted, 43 overlap and 4 wrong. These are instance counts, not an independent population error rate: the three dev draws reuse the same articles and one source pair appears twice. The three different source-pair cases are: production/forecast versus commercial deliveries; revenue-level forecasts versus growth figures whose relation is not established by the records; and a cloud-provider revenue-share description versus an article describing a developer future-sales share. Same source or topic does not prove their specific statements identical. Source accuracy is separate from what a news report actually says. Reader/model disagreement remains and no historical label is changed. Raw source and count: `stored-census.md` and run-specific `merge-third-answer.json`, `library.json`, `decisions.json`.

The observed mechanism is that Jev selects repeat and the writer groups accordingly. The model does not produce a verbal account; the reason for these decisions is unproven. Some records bundle multiple related facts. The issue is not uniquely a low score: the cloud/developer case was selected at 0.84 in one draw. On the 363 fixed saved decisions a 0.5 floor would block one reader-marked wrong merge, four reader-accepted merges and one overlap; this is not a forward-run estimate. In an earlier 102-merge diagnostic an overly strict 'nothing new' rule reduced merges to 22, including valid retellings. Numbers are diagnostic, not an efficacy claim.

## One candidate to investigate

Before grouping a pair that Jev says is a repeat, obtain an independent comparison, with the same source-backed input and without Jev's selection or probabilities: does the incoming statement actually report the old record's main statement? The checker must allow extra details and paraphrases and distinguish different facts, changed claims and cases whose relation cannot be established. This is a proposal for an experiment, not an established root fix, change to D381, a new automatic veto, or proof that another model's errors are independent. We do not choose a model or a disagreement rule in this council.

Use original speaker, the subject, values, period, original date, hedges and actual source when relevant; do not infer the same original claim solely from similar topic, a matching number or common announcement. Different reporting outlets can repeat the same claim while retaining each source. Do not silently adopt D248 boundary 7's dormant exception or a new threshold. Current Jev comparison text excludes an explicit evidence-period field; adding it would be a separate changed input, not silently mixed into this comparison.

The reviewer must not treat a genuine extra detail as automatically disqualifying; X47 is an accepted example. Conversely a broad shared topic or a shared minor fact need not make a whole new record a repeat; X22 and AWS/three-cloud overlap are controls, with source-backed classifications and disagreement. The acceptance reference and Step 2 use different meanings/units for revision in X22; that concern stays separate and the frozen reference remains unchanged. The source itself does not show that the old production statement and the delivery claim were separate statements by the same original speaker, so the revision label is not settled by this case.

## Evidence that would decide whether to proceed

1. Start with a small, predeclared diagnostic of the three reader-marked wrong source pairs and counterexamples: accepted repeats with added details (including X44 and X47), true updates/denials, different speakers/periods, and known missed repeats. Use the identical Jev comparison payload for the independent comparator. It sees no prior result. **方向：** 对一次已完成运行里 Jev 发出的全部修订边，做一次完整清点。
- 选 D392 d1：56 个 supersedes 回答，涉及 34 条记录。

- 每一对同时记录：读者判断时用到的关键原文，是否就在比较文本里。
- 这是这一轮的全体修订边，不是挑选出来的样本；但它只是一轮，用的文章和 dev 有重叠，回答之间也高度聚集。

**它要回答的三个决定性问题：**
1. **有没有至少一条"后来改变"的有效修订被两位读者认可？** 也就是同一说话人改了指引或预测，而且时间先后在原文里成立。

2. **不被支持的边是否集中在"一条否认挂满多条边"上？**

   - 是：这类错是判断错误。
   - 否：这类错只能从输入或记录边界那一侧去研究。

# Step 2: should Jev see retrieval scores?

Research council, 2026-11-08. Scope: the isolated clean Step 2 evidence-comparison path. No production change, model test, or change to the concurrent Step 1 experiment.

## Conclusion

Neither a benefit nor harm has been established. Keep the present request until a controlled comparison shows an advantage. Similarity is calculated between a search query and a stored group's original text; it is not a probability of same statement. The query may contain a thesis and a candidate may have several scores from different queries. Jev does not receive these scores; it receives the incoming piece as state and one candidate per typed question. It returns a choice and probabilities. Jev's choice probability, not cosine, selects among multiple same-statement results.

## Concrete observation

In saved c6 X4, incoming 12:e1 was grouped into 1:E1 although the two revenue-sharing arrangements were judged different. Recomputed from the cached exact-text vectors, cosine of the one thesis query against 1:E1's document is 0.8574. Its own document-vector cosine is 0.8654, but the record had one thesis query and that value was not its retrieval query. The saved Jev answer called same_statement at 0.89. This is one error; it neither establishes that score information will harm Jev nor measures a score distribution. Source: `poc/data/clean-step2-forward-c6-2026-11-08/{decisions.json,library.json,embeddings.json,merge-key.json,merge-third-answer.json}`. Query/doc text and cosine are reconstructed as `clean-arch/step2/compare.py` defines them.

## Council

Claude Code session 4c06c24f-8f77-4add-9443-7081a27b7903; original handoff, streams, stderr and challenge are saved alongside this record. Claude initially recommended an offline score-separation gate. Codex challenged it: overlapping marginal scores cannot rule out conditional help, and separation cannot establish Jev uses them. Claude agreed and withdrew that gate, its extrapolation of score ranges from another task, and claims about Jev's internal reasoning. Offline profiling can inform a test but cannot establish efficacy. Vendor describes Jev as a typed, non-text-generating decision model with independently evaluated questions (https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction); evidence on LLM anchoring is only a hypothesis for Jev, not a finding (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.01724).

## Proposed discriminating test, not yet registered or run

Reconstruct identical saved candidate requests; interleave fresh no-score controls with true-score requests and a score-shuffled control, with fixed score representation and randomization, repeated draws, cache misses, and identical model, candidates and question content except score lines. Make each score's query origin explicit: multiple search queries may yield different scores. A shuffled control tests sensitivity to a number but needs care with singleton/equal-score cases and preserving query origin. A source-blind independent reader judges differing pairs and controls without seeing arm, score, or prior decision. Report wrong merges, missed repeats, incorrect revision classifications and group choices separately, all cases, with same-arm variability, cost and limitations; fixed-candidate comparisons do not prove forward-run performance. The fresh set has few or no revisions; use separately identified stored revision cases without presenting isolated pair results as product-path evidence. Freeze design, audit and preflight under repository rules before any paid send. A score can also encode context Jev did not directly receive (e.g. thesis wording or period), so improvement would not itself establish the mechanism.

No evidence supports a universal score threshold. This proposal does not alter the accepted configuration or authorize deployment.
# Jev retrieval score probe: interrupted; partial result

Alex requested a small council test of whether supplying embedding scores helps Jev. The isolated probe used fixed archived c8 inputs, 11 selected cases, two arms (original control, and real cosine metadata plus query type), 3 same-day draws per arm. It was not a new acceptance measurement, was not a forward run, and cannot measure a change in retrieval recall. The design, frozen manifest and hashes, preflight and source-blind review are in this folder. Frozen rulers, production and the concurrent Step 1 configuration did not change.

## Status

The seventh case's first dispatch (`18:e2`, treatment draw 1) failed with `ConnectionResetError` after 36 successful answers. Whether that request reached the service is unknown. Per the predeclared single-attempt stop rule it was not retried; 29 further planned calls were not sent. Six cases have all six answers; five cases have no complete paired result. In particular the known wrong merge (`22:ev-11`) and revision-bearing example (`19:ev-guidance-70`) were not reached. Six completed cases carry 46 candidate comparisons; control and treatment each have three decisions per candidate. Logged successful input tokens 136,590, logged cost $0.005742; the ambiguous request's actual billing is unknown.

## Observed outcome

Every one of the 46 candidate relation choices was identical in all six draws. The resulting groups and revision links were also identical in all six: 3:e1 repeat of 1:e3; 5:e1 new; 9:e1 new; 9:e6 repeat of 7:E1; 13:e11 repeat of 6:e1; 14:e3 repeat of 7:E4. No revision links occurred. For 5 of the 46 candidate comparisons, the mean reported same-statement probability differed across the arms; one example was 9:e6 against 7:E1, control 0.77/0.74/0.79, treatment 0.84/0.84/0.86. Probabilities do not establish accuracy or explain a cause.

Two independent blind readers each read source materials and all 46 candidates for these cases, and agreed: 3 same, 42 different, 1 overlap. In particular 13:e11 groups a three-cloud growth record into an AWS-only record; both blind readers call it an overlap. Do not count that as unambiguously right or wrong. The other three repeat targets were both called same, and both new cases had no candidates called same or revision. Later details remain preserved as member text; the score does not fix the overlap.

## Interpretation and stop

No visible decision benefit or harm in the six completed selected cases. This is not evidence of equivalence or a measured precision/recall change. The wrong-merge case central to the prediction and the revision-bearing case were not run. The score input also adds query-type metadata and can encode thesis/period content missing from the comparator; an effect could not be attributed to numerical similarity alone. Complete result and two source-backed reviews do not exist for the intended 11 cases. Stop and report the interruption, no automatic resumption or replacement of the ambiguous call. The independent Codex partial review is `partial-review.out`; independent Claude follow-up is `partial-claude.jsonl`. No adoption or product change is justified by these results.

Council post-read: Codex and Claude independently agreed on the six completed outcomes and their limits. Claude's partial review says 106 total candidates across eleven cases; the frozen packet and complete blind annotations contain 96, so 106 is a counting error and is not used. The three reader disagreements lie in unfinished cases. The connection reset's cause is not established; the logged exception is its type only.
# Council: the fresh Step 2 wrong merge (X22)

Read-only council, 2026-11-09. Codex and Claude Code independently traced the sources, the stored Jev request and answer, the Step 3 group and the reader's text; challenge round in `round2.jsonl`. Original user-requested scope: this one error, no product or ruler edits, no paid model calls.

## What happened

The earlier 2026-09-05 Motley Fool source reported that Vera Rubin was in production and that management expected it to represent about 20% of Q3 data-centre revenue. The later 2026-09-06 Calcalist source reported that Nvidia said Vera Rubin systems were commercially delivered in August. The two source articles are preserved in `reports/step2-score-council-2026-11-08/blind-packets.json`, case 9 candidate C7 (key in blind-key.json); these are media reports, not the primary earnings-call transcript.

Archived request for incoming 22:ev-11 against 13:e4 asked Jev to compare their source-backed text. It chose same_statement at 0.49, different 0.36, supersedes 0.15. `clean-arch/step2/compare.py:109` acts on the chosen label without a 0.5 floor, so the incoming record joined 13:e4. Retrieval found this candidate. The model provides no textual explanation; the reason for the choice is unproven.

The fresh merge review classified the two as different, and a third classified the merge wrong. Independent Codex review agrees; earlier Claude blind review called it overlap, and a separate Claude adjudicator called it different. Thus whether it is a clearly wrong merge rather than an overlap depends on reader judgment. We agree the delivery is not a straightforward repeat of the production statement and revenue forecast. The prior acceptance reference grouped underlying article matters as a later step and marked the delivery revision; that reference uses a broader revision concept than Step 2's comparison, and its unit is the article matter, not necessarily the system record. The most natural reading under the current comparison contract is a separate new statement; revision is a plausible interpretation of the milestone depending on the meaning of 'changed event-progress statement'. The primary statement of the original bundled production-and-forecast record is not formally identified. No change to the reference or contract is proposed.

## Actual and potential impact

The clean prototype group retains the delivery record's own summary, quote and source as a member. Offline calling `group_text` on the saved group produces the label 'Later reports of the same statement' above that member: misleading grouping and label, not observed text deletion. The acceptance did not test whether this group changed a reader's investment judgment; Step 4 of this clean path was not built for this run. The production writer and live application were not changed. If a future reader treats group members as restatements, it could underweight a new milestone; that downstream consequence is a risk, not an observed result. The first article attributes the 20% forecast to management but does not explicitly attribute production status to Nvidia; its stored summary does, an attribution difference in this case without an established census.

## A tempting threshold

An offline read of the 57 saved merges showed 2 selected repeats below 0.5: X22 at 0.49 (judged wrong by the original merge readers) and X47 at 0.47 (accepted by both original readers; Broadcom revenue forecasts). A 0.5 floor on this fixed draw would remove one wrong merge and one accepted merge. This is not a root cause proof or general performance measurement. No threshold change is recommended from this single comparison; old production code uses such a floor, while the clean prototype does not, and no decision about adding it to the clean path was established here.

Relevant records: `poc/data/clean-acceptance-2026-11-09/step2/decisions.json`, `library.json`, `jev.sqlite`, `merge-third-answer.json`; `poc/data/clean-acceptance-2026-11-09/settled.json` and `prerun-prompt.md`; `clean-arch/step3/library.py`; `clean-arch/step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/LOG.md` §§43–44. The independent Codex review is `codex-review.md`. One full fresh test produced 1 clear wrong merge of 57 by its readers; this council did not reclassify its immutable result.
# Step 2 wrong-merge council: candidate direction, not a proven fix

2026-11-09. Alex requested a council to think through a general fix. Codex and Claude independently read the saved requests, source-backed records, decisions, current contracts and prior trials, challenged each other's proposals, and converged after further challenges. This is a read-only investigation; no model experiment, production/configuration change, new ruler, or change to the concurrent end-to-end run was made. Streams and handoffs are preserved in this directory.

## What was found

In one fresh draw and three dev draws, 363 accepted-as-repeat outcomes received recorded reviews: 316 accepted, 43 overlap and 4 wrong. These are instance counts, not an independent population error rate: the three dev draws reuse the same articles and one source pair appears twice. The three different source-pair cases are: production/forecast versus commercial deliveries; revenue-level forecasts versus growth figures whose relation is not established by the records; and a cloud-provider revenue-share description versus an article describing a developer future-sales share. Same source or topic does not prove their specific statements identical. Source accuracy is separate from what a news report actually says. Reader/model disagreement remains and no historical label is changed. Raw source and count: `stored-census.md` and run-specific `merge-third-answer.json`, `library.json`, `decisions.json`.

The observed mechanism is that Jev selects repeat and the writer groups accordingly. The model does not produce a verbal account; the reason for these decisions is unproven. Some records bundle multiple related facts. The issue is not uniquely a low score: the cloud/developer case was selected at 0.84 in one draw. On the 363 fixed saved decisions a 0.5 floor would block one reader-marked wrong merge, four reader-accepted merges and one overlap; this is not a forward-run estimate. ## 5. Step 2: find and compare related evidence

### Why this is separate

An open thesis may accumulate many evidence records. Step 1 needs to understand the article and the open research; it does not need to read every prior statement to do that. Step 2 uses each proposed `{thesis, evidence}` association to find the history worth comparing.

### Find candidate evidence

The proposed design places semantic search over the evidence library. It uses the thesis and incoming evidence to find top-N related evidence across the current entity, including evidence linked to other theses. The thesis is search context, not a restriction to evidence already linked to that thesis. This also applies when the proposed thesis is new. For example, “raised its revenue outlook” and “expects higher sales” can be related despite different wording. Alex chose this entity-wide scope on 2026-11-06.

Search returns **candidates**, not a final decision. Alex discussed a starting point of top 10; the implementation and quality requirements need to be measured.

A match outside the returned set will not be considered by the comparison. Search quality therefore matters independently from the model's ability to compare the records it receives.

### Compare with Jev

**2026-11-08 (candidate, [round log](step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/LOG.md) §§24, 31–35):**
- Comparison reads the full passages; the 600-character cut is removed.
- An unlinked record also searches by its own text.
- `figures` never enter a search or comparison text.
- Jev is asked the clean path's own piece question, aligned with line 2's test: a repeat reports the stored piece's main statement, and
  an official's denial of a report is a revision.
- When a thesis opens, every stored unlinked group from earlier articles is judged against it in batches of ten (a yes/no question; the
  company's overall results inform only a revenue or earnings thesis). Each judged pair is recorded once.
- On c6's records: search 97.9%, wrong merges 1.9% (2 of 104), both lines met; line 3 not re-measured.

Jev compares the new evidence with the returned evidence. The intended outcomes are:

| Outcome | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Repeat | The new material presents the same statement again. | Another article reports the same company forecast. |
| Revision | A later account changes the same statement. | The company revises its forecast from 12% to 25%. |
| New evidence | It is not identified as a repeat or revision of the evidence compared. | A different analyst offers a separate forecast. |

The words, amount, speaker, source and time can matter to the comparison. A later statement about the same subject is not necessarily a revision. A matching amount alone does not prove that two statements are the same.

The result “new evidence” is the outcome of the comparison performed; it is not proof that no matching evidence exists elsewhere in the library. When the incoming evidence is judged a repeat of several candidates, it joins only the group Jev judges it most like: the highest same-statement probability, with ties going to the earliest group (Alex, 2026-11-08). A comparison that fails is not saved and is reported.

**Repeat handoff:** when Jev identifies a repeat, the comparison must retain the identity of the existing evidence record it was compared against. Step 3 uses that identity to place the incoming record in the existing record's group, adding its source and any missing thesis link. The typed Jev response need not generate the record ID: the caller can associate the choice with the candidate it supplied. The rule for several matching candidates is stated above.

**Step 2 acceptance (Alex, 2026-11-08).** Three lines apply:
1. For incoming evidence whose earlier version is in the library, search returns it at least 90% of the time.
2. At most 2% of merges are clearly wrong.
3. Grouped dossiers keep no fewer details added by later reports than no merging does.

The first measurement against these lines is in the [Step 2 log](step2-validation-2026-11-07/LOG.md) §12; the isolated modules are `step2/compare.py` and `step3/library.py`.

The diagram's intended sequence is: use `{thesis, incoming evidence}` to search the evidence library; pass the returned candidates and incoming evidence to Jev; pass the comparison result and the proposed association to Step 3. For a new thesis, search the same entity-wide evidence library. A concrete working draft of the Jev comparison request appears in [section 13](#13-step-2-prompt-jev-working-draft).

## 6. Step 3: save evidence and links

Step 3 takes the proposals from Step 1 and the comparison outcomes from Step 2 and writes the resulting research information.

| Result | What is saved |
|---|---|
| New thesis with supporting evidence | The new thesis and its evidence link; save new evidence or reuse a matching record according to Step 2. |
| New evidence for an existing thesis | The evidence and its link to the thesis. |
| Repeat | Place the incoming record in the existing evidence record's group: add its source and any missing link to the relevant thesis, and keep the incoming record's own text and fields inside the group. Do not rewrite the existing record, and do not create a separate evidence record for the same statement. |
| Revision | The new evidence and its source, linked to the earlier statement as a revision. |

A revision does not erase the earlier statement. On 2026-11-06, Alex chose to keep one evidence record for a repeat and add the new source and any missing thesis link. On 2026-11-08 the Step 2 validation showed that keeping only the earlier text discards details a later report adds, such as a guidance condition; Alex then chose to keep each repeat's own text and source inside the stored record's group, without rewriting the original ("A 继续；跑council loop 开始做"; [Step 2 log](step2-validation-2026-11-07/LOG.md) §7). How a judgement reads a group is being tested. Multiple articles reporting the same statement do not automatically establish independent original sources. The current production writer stores separate repeat records, so this is a change for the clean path and needs implementation and verification; the existing historical records remain available. Step 3 ends when the chosen thesis, evidence and relationships are saved. How they are physically stored and written is a separate implementation decision.

## Independent readings

**T01 — `same_statement`.** Both articles attribute the same fiscal 2027 and 2028 AI chip revenue outlook to Broadcom. The incoming source says “about $115 billion” for fiscal 2027 and “roughly $230 billion” for fiscal 2028; the stored source says “$115 billion” and “$230 billion” for those years. Both articles are dated September 6. The incoming record adds customers and says the 2027 forecast was raised from over $100 billion; those details do not establish a different main forecast. Neither article supplies the exact day of the underlying statement.

**T02 — `different`.** The stored record’s main statement is that Kress said **customer forecasts** indicated revenue “may double next year.” The incoming record’s main statement is the company’s **70% fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast**. The stored article itself separately reports both: the 70% guidance and the customer-demand indication. The incoming article also says unconstrained growth could be “a lot higher” than 70%, but that overlap with the stored record’s secondary Huang statement does not make the main statements identical. The incoming $673 billion–$700 billion figure is the article’s calculation from consensus, not a separately attributed Nvidia forecast. The articles were published September 5 and 6; that order does not establish a revision of customer demand.

**T03 — `supersedes`.** The stored main claim is SemiAnalysis’s report that “Kyber NVL144 rack architecture has been delayed to 2028.” The incoming article reports that Nvidia “rejected the claims” and said its roadmap remains intact. That is a direct official denial of the main delay claim under the requested definition. It does not prove which party is right or specifically settle the stored record’s secondary NVL576 claim. The stored article already contains Nvidia’s denial, so this is not necessarily a newly issued response. Its publication metadata says July 5 while its text and URL refer to Monday, July 6; the precise sequence is therefore uncertain.

**T04 — `same_statement`.** Both articles report Nvidia’s Thursday announcement of a Hugging Face acquisition: the stored article calls it a “$12.9 billion deal to purchase,” while the incoming article says “$13 billion.” The amounts are compatible with rounding, and the parties and announced transaction match. The incoming September 6 article refers to reporting by EU Tech Loop and Euronews; the stored article is dated September 5. “Acquisition” in the incoming wording does not establish that the deal closed, and neither record establishes regulatory approval.

**T05 — `different`.** The stored main statement says Vera Rubin is “already in production” and forecasts about **20% of data-center revenue** in fiscal Q3. The incoming statement says systems based on Vera Rubin “had already been delivered commercially to customers during August 2026.” Production and commercial delivery are related stages, but they are distinct claims; delivery does not confirm or replace the 20% forecast. Both reports attribute their information to Nvidia around the earnings call, but the article dates alone do not prove that the underlying statements were made on different days.

**T06 — `different`, with a boundary ambiguity.** The stored article’s main conclusion is that the base Shield TV **appears** discontinued, based on retail availability; it explicitly says it could “simply be an out-of-stock situation.” The later article quotes Nvidia: the base model is “largely out of stock due to demand” and it has “no updates” on future availability. Nvidia neither confirms nor denies discontinuation. The July 13 article also reports that B&H changed its status from “discontinued” to “No Longer Available.” It describes the future as “in limbo,” but does not explicitly retract the July 8 article’s qualified conclusion. I therefore read the official response as a distinct statement. There is a reasonable unresolved boundary over whether the same publisher’s later, more cautious framing should count as changing its earlier main statement.

## Status

The seventh case's first dispatch (`18:e2`, treatment draw 1) failed with `ConnectionResetError` after 36 successful answers. Whether that request reached the service is unknown. Per the predeclared single-attempt stop rule it was not retried; 29 further planned calls were not sent. Six cases have all six answers; five cases have no complete paired result. Every one of the 46 candidate relation choices was identical in all six draws. The resulting groups and revision links were also identical in all six: 3:e1 repeat of 1:e3; 5:e1 new; 9:e1 new; 9:e6 repeat of 7:E1; 13:e11 repeat of 6:e1; 14:e3 repeat of 7:E4. No visible decision benefit or harm in the six completed selected cases. This is not evidence of equivalence or a measured precision/recall change. # Step 2 wrong-merge council: candidate direction, not a proven fix

2026-11-09. Alex requested a council to think through a general fix. Codex and Claude independently read the saved requests, source-backed records, decisions, current contracts and prior trials, challenged each other's proposals, and converged after further challenges. This is a read-only investigation; no model experiment, production/configuration change, new ruler, or change to the concurrent end-to-end run was made. Streams and handoffs are preserved in this directory.

## What was found

In one fresh draw and three dev draws, 363 accepted-as-repeat outcomes received recorded reviews: 316 accepted, 43 overlap and 4 wrong. These are instance counts, not an independent population error rate: the three dev draws reuse the same articles and one source pair appears twice. The three different source-pair cases are: production/forecast versus commercial deliveries; revenue-level forecasts versus growth figures whose relation is not established by the records; and a cloud-provider revenue-share description versus an article describing a developer future-sales share. Same source or topic does not prove their specific statements identical. Source accuracy is separate from what a news report actually says. Reader/model disagreement remains and no historical label is changed. Raw source and count: `stored-census.md` and run-specific `merge-third-answer.json`, `library.json`, `decisions.json`.

The observed mechanism is that Jev selects repeat and the writer groups accordingly. The model does not produce a verbal account; the reason for these decisions is unproven. Some records bundle multiple related facts. The issue is not uniquely a low score: the cloud/developer case was selected at 0.84 in one draw. On the 363 fixed saved decisions a 0.5 floor would block one reader-marked wrong merge, four reader-accepted merges and one overlap; this is not a forward-run estimate. In an earlier 102-merge diagnostic an overly strict 'nothing new' rule reduced merges to 22, including valid retellings. Numbers are diagnostic, not an efficacy claim.

## One candidate to investigate

Before grouping a pair that Jev says is a repeat, obtain an independent comparison, with the same source-backed input and without Jev's selection or probabilities: does the incoming statement actually report the old record's main statement? The checker must allow extra details and paraphrases and distinguish different facts, changed claims and cases whose relation cannot be established. This is a proposal for an experiment, not an established root fix, change to D381, a new automatic veto, or proof that another model's errors are independent. We do not choose a model or a disagreement rule in this council.

Use original speaker, the subject, values, period, original date, hedges and actual source when relevant; do not infer the same original claim solely from similar topic, a matching number or common announcement. Different reporting outlets can repeat the same claim while retaining each source. Do not silently adopt D248 boundary 7's dormant exception or a new threshold. Current Jev comparison text excludes an explicit evidence-period field; adding it would be a separate changed input, not silently mixed into this comparison.

The reviewer must not treat a genuine extra detail as automatically disqualifying; X47 is an accepted example. Conversely a broad shared topic or a shared minor fact need not make a whole new record a repeat; X22 and AWS/three-cloud overlap are controls, with source-backed classifications and disagreement. The acceptance reference and Step 2 use different meanings/units for revision in X22; that concern stays separate and the frozen reference remains unchanged. The source itself does not show that the old production statement and the delivery claim were separate statements by the same original speaker, so the revision label is not settled by this case.

## Evidence that would decide whether to proceed

1. Start with a small, predeclared diagnostic of the three reader-marked wrong source pairs and counterexamples: accepted repeats with added details (including X44 and X47), true updates/denials, different speakers/periods, and known missed repeats. Use the identical Jev comparison payload for the independent comparator. It sees no prior result. A source-blind reader who did not write the proposal reviews the source and differences; same-day fresh Jev controls and request fidelity are required for model comparisons. A small pilot is a lead, not a performance claim.
2. If the pilot provides an actual signal without obvious counterexample regressions, prospectively freeze an expanded evaluation of all 363 historical merged instances and known missed repeats and revisions, marking the model-written judgments and 43 contested overlaps; do not relabel frozen gold or infer that 363 are independent. Assess wrong groupings, correct repeats split, unmerged repeats, update errors and source fidelity; give every case and disagreement. Fixed-history comparison cannot establish new forward-history behavior, latency or downstream judgment impact.
3. Only if those comparisons merit it, plan a separate isolated forward-path evaluation with a fresh same-day baseline, held-out articles and eventual reader/judgment effects, including cost and speed. Do not use the 50 fresh-test articles as previously unseen again. No new scorer substitutes for source-backed trace review.

A useful test must show the independent comparison catches cases Jev misses without unnecessarily breaking true repeats or losing/relabeling updates. If errors are correlated, correct repeats are split, or the model's additional cost exceeds the observed value, do not adopt it. The pilot may be inconclusive, especially with few confirmed wrong pairs. It cannot prove absence of a problem.

Whether a reviewer disagreement creates a new group, a pending case or some other outcome changes product behavior; it is not decided by the council and must be shown to Alex with evidence. Likewise source-matter revision vs statement revision and risk trade-offs need an explicit decision if the existing rules do not resolve them. The final delivered investment judgment has not been shown to suffer from X22; the currently running July end-to-end comparison does not contain this September case and cannot isolate this merge.

**判断：不同。** 新记录是 Nvidia 对缺货情况的新回应，涉及同一台设备，但没有重复、正式确认或否认旧记录的主要判断：标准版 Shield TV 似乎已经停产。这是基于所给材料的独立意见，不是金标。

旧文章于 **2026 年 7 月 8 日**由 Pocket-lint 的 Craig Donaldson 发表。它的主要判断是：标准版 Shield TV 的销售寿命似乎已经结束，Nvidia “**seems to have quietly discontinued it**”，并注明这一线索来自 **AFTV News**。但文章同时明确留有余地：“**it’s possible this is simply an out-of-stock situation**”。当时 Pocket-lint 尚未得到 Nvidia 的正式确认，并表示已向公司询问。

新文章于 **2026 年 7 月 13 日**由同一出版方、同一作者发表，报道了 Nvidia 的邮件回复。Nvidia 说：

> “The SHIELD TV base model is largely out of stock due to demand. We don't have any updates to share regarding future availability at this time.”

Nvidia 还说 Pro 版仍有售，Shield 平台继续获得更新。**这些是 Nvidia 的正式回应，但不是对停产问题的正式回答**：缺货原因被归为需求旺盛，未来是否补货以及设备是否停产，都没有得到明确答复。文章也写道，公司 “**sidestepped whether the device has been discontinued**”。

这两篇文章之间确实有变化：7 月 8 日，作者认为停产迹象很强；7 月 13 日，作者说设备的未来 “**remains in limbo**”。但后文没有说 Pocket-lint 或 AFTV News 撤回或更正了早先的判断。后文提到的是零售商 **B&H** 把商品状态从 “**discontinued**” 改为 “**No Longer Available**”；这是零售商标签的变化，不能当作出版方撤稿，也不能当作 Nvidia 否认停产。

另一种合理解释是把新文章看成对旧报道的**后续更新**：同一作者拿到了先前等待的公司回应，也用了更谨慎的措辞。但它没有明确修正旧判断，因此如果要判断两条记录所表达的主要声明，较合适的是“不同”；真正的停产状态仍然**不确定**。

两条记录都把 `original_party` 写成 Nvidia，但旧文章的停产判断是 **Pocket-lint 引述 AFTV News 并根据零售商情况作出的推断**，不是 Nvidia 的声明。新记录才有直接归属于 Nvidia 的邮件内容。两条记录都没有给出 Nvidia 具体发言日期；**7 月 8 日和 7 月 13 日是文章发表日期**，不能据此断定邮件是在 7 月 13 日发出的。**P01 对 `45:e3` 的修订链接应标为“有争议”，不能算已验证正确。** 因此，P01 的目标关系答对了，不能说明这条记录写出的所有关系都正确。

`45:e3` 的主陈述是：SemiAnalysis 报道，两机柜拼接的备用方案被取消，并认为 Nvidia 缺少经过验证的扩展方案。新文章先报道 Kyber 延期，**也提到了同一备用方案被取消**，然后说 Nvidia 拒绝了“这些说法”。这使较宽的否认解读有一定依据；但 Nvidia 的实际表述只是“路线图完好”，没有具体说明是否否认备用方案取消，也没有逐项回应扩展方案问题。两篇都属转述，原始回应时间不清楚。

实际 Jev 请求中的新记录只概括为 Nvidia 拒绝“延期说法”，没有带上新文章提到备用方案的上下文。按现行规则，只有回应了旧记录的**主陈述**才算修订；是否可以把这句宽泛回应扩展到 `45:e3`，现有材料不足以确定。见 [完整来源 P01](/Users/lchingen/hivemind-step2-identity-2026-11-09/clean-arch/step2-identity-2026-11-09/blind-positive-revisions.json)、[完整 Jev 请求，P01 q2](/Users/lchingen/hivemind-step2-identity-2026-11-09/clean-arch/step2-identity-2026-11-09/probe-2026-11-09/bodies.json) 和 [比较规则](/Users/lchingen/hivemind-step2-identity-2026-11-09/clean-arch/step2/compare.py:57)。

三次完整 Jev 回答都把新记录放进 `45:e2`，同时连向 `45:e1` 和 `45:e3`。盲读对照只审了 `45:e1`，所以它支持的是 **`45:e1` 这条关系的判断**，不是整个写入结果的正确性。独立比较器也只回答了 `45:e1` 这一对。见 [结果重放](/Users/lchingen/hivemind-step2-identity-2026-11-09/clean-arch/step2-identity-2026-11-09/RESULTS-DRAFT.md)。

**R05 我也要收窄之前的结论。** 我仍倾向于“不属于修订”：Nvidia 解释了缺货，但没有确认或否认停产。新的盲读指出，同一家媒体后来采用了更谨慎的表述，且零售商更改了商品状态；这使“后续报道是否改变了原推测”存在合理边界争议。因此，独立比较器的 `different` 是**有来源支持的改善线索**，不应再称为无争议地纠正了错误链接。见 [结果盲读 T06](/Users/lchingen/hivemind-step2-identity-2026-11-09/clean-arch/step2-identity-2026-11-09/result-blind-codex.md)。

By Craig Donaldson
In 2019, Nvidia launched two new Shield TV streaming devices: the Shield TV and Shield TV Pro. Even though they're now more than six years old, both have remained popular, especially among enthusiasts who appreciate their powerful hardware and the freedom that comes with Android TV.
Recently, though, concerns have been growing about the future of the cheaper $150 Shield TV. While the $200 Shield TV Pro remains widely available, stock of the cheaper Shield TV has disappeared from major retailers like Amazon, Best Buy, and Newegg, with no indication it's coming back. B&H Photo Video even labeled the Shield TV as "discontinued" before recently changing the product status to "No Longer Available," fueling speculation that Nvidia has quietly pulled the plug on the device.
Pocket-lint reached out to Nvidia for clarification on the Shield TV's future and received an email response. Here's what Nvidia had to say:
"The SHIELD TV base model is largely out of stock due to demand. We don't have any updates to share regarding future availability at this time. SHIELD TV Pro remains available, and the SHIELD platform continues to be supported with ongoing updates for more than 10 years."
Nvidia won't say the Shield TV is discontinued
But it's not confirming that it's coming back either
While Nvidia confirmed that the base Shield TV is out of stock due to demand, what's still unclear is what happens next.
In its email response to Pocket-lint, the company sidestepped whether the device has been discontinued, saying only that it has no updates to share regarding its availability. That makes it seem like Nvidia isn't ready to say the Shield TV has been discontinued, but it also isn't willing to confirm that it's coming back. As a result, the future of the base Shield TV remains in limbo.
I wouldn't be surprised if the Shield TV's stock situation is tied to the ongoing global memory shortage. Component prices have risen significantly over the past year as AI data centers have snapped up huge amounts of RAM and storage, and Nvidia likely isn't in a great position to manufacture more Shield TVs without raising the device's $150 price tag. This is purely speculation on my part, but it could explain why Nvidia doesn't want to definitively rule out producing more Shield TVs just yet.
Another reason Nvidia might not be in a rush to restock the base Shield TV is the continued availability of the $200 Shield TV Pro . In its statement, the company confirmed that the Pro model "remains available," and if it still has ample inventory, it would make sense for Nvidia to shift its focus to that device instead. After all, the Shield TV Pro is the better option and more popular anyway, thanks to its extra RAM and storage, USB ports, Gigabit Ethernet, and support for 64-bit apps.
Nvidia hasn't ruled out a new Shield TV either
This whole situation surrounding the base Shield TV's availability, and whether it'll ever come back, has also gotten me thinking about whether Nvidia will ever release new Shield TV models. Both the Shield TV and Shield TV Pro are now more than six years old, and they're long overdue for a refresh.
Nvidia hasn't officially confirmed any plans for new Shield TV hardware, but it also hasn't ruled out the possibility.
In an interview with Ars Technica back in January, Nvidia's Senior VP of Hardware Engineering, Andrew Bell, was asked about the possibility of future Shield TV models. His response was encouraging:
"We talk about it all the time -- I'd love to."
Bell went on to say that if Nvidia comes up with a new Shield TV concept the company is passionate about, it could happen.
Overall, the future of the base Shield TV remains uncertain, as does whether Nvidia will ever release new Shield TV models. What is clear, though, is that if you're looking to buy a Shield TV today, the Shield TV Pro is your best bet. Nvidia also has no plans to stop supporting its existing Shield TV lineup, with software updates continuing to roll out occasionally.

By Craig Donaldson
Although it's been more than six years since they launched in 2019, Nvidia's Shield TV and Shield TV Pro have remained two of the most popular streaming devices on the market, especially among power users, and for good reason.

That said, the regular Shield TV was still a compelling option. At $150, it costs $50 less than the Shield TV Pro while still delivering the same speedy Nvidia Tegra X1+ processor. If you didn't need the extra RAM or storage, it was an easy way to get most of the Shield experience for less.
Unfortunately, it now appears that the cheaper Shield TV's time on the market has come to an end, as Nvidia seems to have quietly discontinued it (via AFTV News ). The Shield TV is no longer available to purchase directly from Nvidia, and the same is true across most major retailers.
